description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:791,803,819,832,883,896,924,938 — build_signed_input_x509_entry / build_signed_input_precert_entry / build_merkle_tree_leaf_x509_entry / build_merkle_tree_leaf_precert_entry all do '(sct.extensions.len() as u16).to_be_bytes()'. There's a debug_assert! guarding it but only debug builds catch the overflow.

If a caller (test code, fuzz harness, or future API that constructs SCT from sources other than the wire parser) builds a SignedCertificateTimestamp with extensions.len() > 65535, the cast silently truncates to len() & 0xFFFF. Output bytes carry the wrong u16 length; downstream signature verification fails with InvalidSignature — caller sees a misleading error, not the actual cause.

The parser itself is safe (read_u16_prefixed bounds at u16::MAX). The public struct SignedCertificateTimestamp has 'pub extensions: Vec<u8>' — i.e., any caller can construct it directly with a >u16 vec. Per workspace policy (non-negotiable #6 'cache-friendly' and pre-1.0 'design closure'), the constructor should enforce this invariant or the build_* functions should return an error.

Suggested fix: change debug_assert! to a real check returning Error::ParseError or a new Error::ExtensionsTooLong variant. Cheap, eliminates silent-truncation footgun.
title: build_signed_input_*: u16 cast of sct.extensions.len() silently truncates if caller constructs SCT with >65535 extensions
